analysis.investment_thesis: Embassy Developments scores at the bottom of both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield of ~2.5% (vs. 12%+ threshold) and ROIC of ~3% (vs. 20%+ threshold) — making it fundamentally unqualified for the formula. The business is a real estate developer, a capital-intensive sector Greenblatt explicitly deprioritizes because capital structure distorts both metrics.
key_strengths: Balance sheet massively recapitalized in FY25 — equity surged from -1,446 Cr (2024) to 10,258 Cr (2025), de-risking insolvency concerns
FY25 recovery visible: revenue +84% YoY to 2,180 Cr, EBITDA turned positive to 322 Cr after -501 Cr in FY23
FII ownership of 25.3% suggests some institutional validation of the restructuring thesis
key_risks: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = 293/11,513 Cr ≈ 2.5% — catastrophically below Magic Formula threshold of 12%
ROCE of 3.19% on a 20,857 Cr asset base is capital destruction; ROIC has never sustainably exceeded 5% in the last decade
Massive debt jump from 693 Cr (FY23) to 7,749 Cr (FY24) then 4,599 Cr (FY25) signals leveraged restructuring, not organic strength
red_flags: Net losses in 3 of last 4 years: -137 Cr (FY22), -608 Cr (FY23), -517 Cr (FY24) — EBIT was negative, Magic Formula inapplicable
EV/EBITDA reported as -100.6x (negative EBITDA on trailing basis) — metric is meaningless and confirms earnings quality issues
Operating CF positive only 2 of last 5 years; real estate developer with lumpy, untrustworthy earnings recognition
Revenue CAGR of -3.3% over 9 years — the business is structurally smaller than a decade ago
Name change from Equinox India Developments → Embassy Developments (Feb 2025) mid-restructuring adds opacity
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on EMBDL yields disqualifying numbers on both axes. Enterprise Value = Market Cap (6,983 Cr) + Net Debt (4,530 Cr) = ~11,513 Cr. EBIT (FY25 Operating Income) = 293 Cr. Earnings Yield = 293/11,513 = 2.5% — less than one-fifth of the 12% minimum I look for. Return on Capital = EBIT / invested capital is confirmed by the company's own ROCE of 3.19% — on a bloated 20,857 Cr asset base, the business earns almost nothing. Both legs of the formula are broken simultaneously, which historically predicts poor future returns.

The backstory here is a deeply troubled developer that was losing money from FY22–FY24 (cumulative ~1.26 Cr in losses) and carried negative equity as recently as FY24. The FY25 recapitalization — equity swinging from -1,446 Cr to +10,258 Cr — and the brand relaunch under the Embassy name are corporate actions, not evidence of a high-return business recovering. Real estate developers like this structurally fail the Magic Formula: revenue is lumpy, capital is tied up in land and WIP for years, and returns on that capital are rarely above cost of capital. Until EBIT/EV crosses 10%+ and ROCE exceeds 15% on a sustained basis, this is not a Magic Formula candidate.
